section_summary.extract_value: This section presents a path analysis examining whether social safeness (SSPS) and body appreciation (BAS-2) mediate the relationship between early memories of warmth and safeness with family figures and peers (EMWSS and EMWSS_peers) and disordered eating attitudes (EDE-Q), while controlling for BMI. The final model demonstrated excellent fit and explained 51% of eating psychopathology variance, with all path coefficients statistically significant (p < .001). Results confirmed that both social safeness and body appreciation serve as significant mediators of the impact of early memories on eating disorder symptoms.
